analysis: Phase 9 nested bootstrap CI for optimism-corrected Delta-C

stop_condition_triggered.source: v2.1 section 9.5 -- 'Projected runtime exceeds twice the budget'

diagnosis.detail: The stop condition's stated rationale was that a runtime blow-up would INDICATE a mis-specification. No mis-specification is present: every completed replicate is valid, 0 failures, event/censor composition preserved, pairing intact. The cause is a budgeting error -- the 0.852 s/inner-replicate probe was measured on the original 452-patient data, whereas nested inner fits run on bootstrap samples OF bootstrap samples, with more tied event times and more strained designs, so the ridge inner-CV takes more iterations.
diagnosis.not_thread_oversubscription: each of the 8 workers ran at ~100% CPU = ~800% on 8 cores; no oversubscription to recover

state_preserved.work_lost_on_halt: only in-flight replicates; records are written only when complete

partial_values_are_not_a_result.note: partial outer draws are NOT an interval and are not reported as one

options_for_the_decision_maker: A. RESUME as approved -- 5 runs x B_out 500; ~18.4 h remaining; resume is free and bit-identical; no design change
B. REDUCE the number of runs or B_out -- CHANGES THE APPROVED DESIGN, needs explicit approval, and would weaken the between-run endpoint MC-SE that five runs were chosen to provide
C. ABANDON -- the corrected-Delta-C interval remains unquantified
recommendation: A -- resume unchanged. The computation is correct; only my budget estimate was wrong, and a wrong estimate is not a reason to weaken an approved design.
